study type: Retrospective cohort analysis and predictive model development study
exposure: Maternal characteristics (gestational age, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, body weight, body length, placental weight)
Fetal conditions (preterm birth status, amniotic fluid grade III status, oligohydramnios status, severe small-for-gestational-age status)
outcome: Maternal and fetal outcomes (gestational age, highest systolic and diastolic blood pressure, newborn body weight, newborn body length, placental weight, incidence of preterm birth, amniotic fluid grade III, oligohydramnios, severe small-for-gestational-age neonates)
cohort: The study included 208 pregnant women with pre-eclampsia (PE) complicated with fetal growth restriction (FGR).
finding: The study found no significant difference in the incidence of maternal and fetal complications between different delivery methods, and the three-layer neural network prediction model achieved an accuracy rate of 91.80% for vaginal delivery in this cohort.
mod_finding: There is no significant difference in the incidence of maternal and fetal complications in PE complicated with FGR in different delivery methods.
birth_weight: Newborn body weight was measured and found to be significantly higher in the vaginal delivery group; the cohort included fetuses with growth restriction and severe small-for-gestational-age neonates.
gest_age: Gestational age was measured and found to be significantly higher in the vaginal delivery group; preterm birth was also an outcome measured.
